subject: Post-call: Throughput characterization & SLO clarifications
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Greg Barnes <gbarnes@finster.ai>, Anna Kowalski <anna.k@finster.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Apr 2025 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Throughput characterization & SLO clarifications

Hi Greg / Anna —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and the follow-ups we committed to:

Top-level SLOs you called out:
- P95 latency target: 150 ms (text-generation API, end-to-end)
-99th percentile (tail) target: 350 ms for non-streamed responses
- Streaming required for multi-chunk long responses (>1k tokens) with ~200 ms first-byte target

Workload notes we captured on the call (please confirm):
- Typical request size: ~300 tokens output per call, with ~50 tokens input average
- Typical steady-state QPS: 12 QPS
- Peak spikes: up to 110 QPS sustained for ~2–3 hours/day during batch jobs
- Concurrency: application opens ~40 concurrent model connections during spikes

Action items I promised:
1) Monica / Jonas: draft a throughput-sizing calc based on the 300-token average and the spike profile — deliver Monday.
2) Greg / Anna: share any telemetry you have on tokens-per-request distribution and percent of streaming vs non-streaming traffic (spreadsheet or exported logs).
3) Rafael: propose an initial SLO-compliant config (CPU/GPU pool sizing + caching suggestions) after we get the telemetry.

Attached: finster_request_matrix.xlsx (template) and a short SLO draft (slo_requirements_draft.pdf). Please fill the matrix where possible — we use it to validate tokens/sec and KV-cache hit assumptions.

If anything above is off, correct me in a reply. Planning to run preliminary sizing once we get the matrix.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

--

Attachment: slo_requirements_draft.pdf (PDF, 120KB)

From: Greg Barnes <gbarnes@finster.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Anna Kowalski <anna.k@finster.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Throughput characterization & SLO clarifications

Rafael —

Thanks for the clear recap. Confirming and adding a few specifics from our side:

Confirmed numbers:
- Average output per call: 320 tokens (median ~300, 90th ~520)
- Input tokens: average 60 tokens
- Steady-state: 12 QPS (weekday business hours)
- Regular daily peak: 3-hour window with sustained 95–110 QPS (we see this most days around 09:00–12:00 UTC)
- Short spikes: occasional short bursts to ~200 QPS for a few minutes during test runs
- Streaming share: ~18% of requests use streaming (mostly long reports)
- Concurrency: our app maintains ~35–45 concurrent open inference requests during peak

I've attached an exported sample of our API telemetry (CSV) and completed a few rows of your matrix. The CSV has per-request token counts and timestamps for a 72 hour window.

Couple of notes/questions:
- We rely on relatively low-latency first byte for streamed responses; 200 ms first-byte at p95 is a hard requirement for a subset of workflows.
- Do you recommend keeping separate routes/models for streaming and non-streaming to avoid head-of-line blocking?

Next steps for us: please produce the sizing calc and recommended SLO-aligned configuration. We're aiming to finalize infra budgeting by end of next week.

Greg
Greg Barnes
Head of Infrastructure
Finster Analytics
gbarnes@finster.ai

--
Attachment: finster_api_sample_72h.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Greg Barnes <gbarnes@finster.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Apr 2025 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Throughput characterization & SLO clarifications

Greg — thanks for the dataset. A few quick technical clarifications while Jonas and I start the sizing spreadsheet: 

1) Token/sec vs QPS: for the sizing calc we'll derive tokens/sec by multiplying your average output tokens by expected QPS for each bucket (steady/peak/spike). We'll also estimate effective GPU token throughput under different quantization and batching profiles.

2) Streaming vs non-streaming routing: recommended to separate streaming traffic onto a different route (or model variant) to avoid blocking. For example, a lightweight streaming-optimized model with shorter per-token latency and a dedicated stream queue can keep first-byte targets without impacting non-streamed throughput.

3) KV cache and prefix caching: curious if you expect a high prefix-reuse rate for the long reports (do similar prompts repeat)? If yes, cache hit rates materially reduce token throughput and GPU load. If not, we size assuming low cache benefit.

4) Concurrency handling: do you use an application-level connection pool per user session or per worker? Understanding connection counts helps us size per-worker mem for KV and request queues.

Jonas / I will run two scenarios: conservative (no cache, modest batching, baseline kernels) and optimized (30% cache hit, medium batch sizes, quantized model). We'll attach the calc workbook and a short explanation of assumptions.

Rafael — we'll need a 30–45 minute follow-up to walk through the scenarios. Are you available Wed 16 Apr between 8–11 AM PT?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Throughput characterization & SLO clarifications

Thanks all —

We reviewed internally and filled the matrix with additional percentiles and peak-day logs. A couple clarifications answered here:
- Prefix reuse: low for ad-hoc reports, but templates (about 12% of traffic) reuse similar prefixes — expect ~10–15% cache hit overall
- App connection pooling: per-worker (k8s pod) pool of 8 connections, with ~5 pods active in steady-state and up to 25 pods during the peak window

We'll join the Wed 16 Apr slot — Rafael, the 8:30 AM PT time works for me. Please send calendar invite.

Greg
